jane_auditor: Hi team — for SOC 2 evidence we need a playback for the 'staging' RBAC changes on 2025-11-12. Specifically: who modified role bindings, the KMS-encrypted Snowball import activities, and linked vuln-triage tickets. Also need proof of key rotation and chain-of-custody for artifacts. What exports should we run and how long will this take? cc @maria @tim

maria: Hi Jane — we can assemble CloudTrail (management & data events) + KMS CloudTrail events + k8s audit logs + git PR -> deploy mapping. For Snowball we capture the jobId and S3 object events that reference the import. Plan: 1) CloudTrail export for window, 2) k8s audit snapshot (etcd/audit), 3) KMS key history + GetKeyRotationStatus, 4) link vuln ticket. I can bundle and redact PII.

tim: I can run the CloudTrail & S3 event export. Which exact window? Also confirm if redaction of emails/service-owner names is acceptable.

jane_auditor: Window: 2025-11-12 00:00 -> 2025-11-12 06:00 UTC. Redaction ok as long as ARNs, action names, and artifact hashes remain. Need PR/commit hashes that triggered the RBAC change.

raj: The RBAC change came from a deploy that hit staging at ~00:45. It was applied by service-account deploy-bot via a CI job. I'll pull the k8s audit events and the GitHub PR link.

maria: Good — we'll provide a mapping file: commit -> CI run -> kubectl apply -> k8s audit event -> CloudTrail auth event -> KMS envelope key access. Also include vuln triage ticket #4562 and mitigation notes.

tim: Running queries now. Sample Splunk/Elastic query patterns I will use (copy-paste):

```
# CloudTrail: find KMS decrypts and S3 PutObject events with Snowball jobId
index=cloudtrail eventName=CreateJob OR eventName=ImportKeyMaterial OR eventName=Decrypt
| stats count by eventName, userIdentity.arn, eventTime, requestParameters.jobId
\n# k8s audit: find rolebinding creates/patches
index=k8s_audit verb=patch OR verb=create objectRef.resource=rolebinding
| table eventTime, user.username, objectRef.name, request.object
```

raj: Note: Snowball imports wrap data with an ephemeral envelope key; the KMS events we see are KeyAccess/GenerateDataKey operations for the job. We can supply the KMS GenerateDataKey/Decrypt events with keyId and requestID.

opsbot: export-job started: export-id=x12345, components=[cloudtrail,k8s_audit,kms,git_commits,snowball_metadata], window=2025-11-12T00:00:00Z/2025-11-12T06:00:00Z, ETA=20m. Status link: https://ops.redwood/internal/exports/x12345

jane_auditor: Thanks — also need checksums and manifest proving the artifacts didn't change in transit. And a short chain-of-custody note for the Snowball import.

maria: We'll include SHA256 of each artifact, S3 etags, and a signed manifest (GPG-signed by security). Chain-of-custody will include: Snowball jobId, job manifest, KMS envelope key event IDs, and operator ARNs. Expected package ETA: EOD today.

tim: Export complete. Bundle: https://redwood-secure-files/exports/x12345 (shared with auditor account). Contents: cloudtrail.json.gz, k8s_audit.json.gz, kms_events.json.gz, git_commits.csv, manifest-signed.asc :lock:

jane_auditor: Got the bundle. Quick follow-up — how do you demonstrate key rotation timing? Need evidence the old key was not usable at time-of-access.

maria: We'll include: (a) KMS GetKeyRotationStatus snapshot, (b) CloudTrail KMS DisableKeyRotation/EnableKeyRotation events, (c) CloudTrail CryptoKeyAccess events showing last used timestamps, and (d) ListAliases/GetKeyPolicy outputs for proof of alias re-pointing. Sample aws CLI for evidence: `aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key-id>` and `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=DisableKeyRotation`

raj: Also including the PR that introduced the service-account binding and the CI job logs (kubectl apply stdout). Those will help link the actor identity.

jane_auditor: Perfect. I'll review and follow up with any gaps. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
